UnitStatement: The thesis addresses systems engineering of LLM agent governance for regulated professional practice.
The research question asks how systems engineering principles can govern LLM-based agent systems for reliable use in regulated professional engineering practice.
Epistemic architecture uses mandatory provenance, no-invention, conflict surfacing, and epistemic labeling to respond to the LLM reliability problem.
Regulatory mapping connects APEGA's Relying on the Work of Others guidance directly to AI agent governance.
The thesis frames AI agents as others whose work the professional relies on.
The four-pillar philosophical framework consists of ontology, epistemology, praxiology, and axiology.
The four-pillar philosophical framework is fractally instantiated through the document kit.
Fault containment through write scope uses a Type 0/1/2 hierarchy for formal blast radius containment.
The three-layer invariant system consists of R1-R9, I1-I10, and K-* with a four-layer enforcement map.
All thesis content draws from the Chirality project governance documents.
